newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crudes spike higher on supply disrupts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crudes spike higher on supply disrupts.

text.p: Prices for U.S. cash crudes in the Gulf spiked higher Monday afternoon on supply disruptions in Colombia where rebel attacks on the Cano Limon pipeline resulted in force majeure declarations.
September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 50 cents higher at $20.75-85 a barrel, and put the front month grade even with second month cash levels.

For the second time in three weeks, Colombian rebels effectively bombed a crude pipeline, forcing Cano field production shutdowns. Occidental Petroleum Corp declared force majeure on Cano field output earlier in the day, displacing 175,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude.
West Texas Sour/Midland gained the most from the Cano troubles, selling at a high of $1.32 under WTI/Cushing, from discounts closer to $1.40-45 under on Friday.
Other grades were steady from earlier clockings, with Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James at a 22-25 cents premium to the benchmark and WTI/Cushing Postings Plus at $1.99-2.01.
